b1.note: For web content, usable SharedArrayBuffer requires a secure, cross-origin-isolated context; COOP: same-origin plus COEP: require-corp is the usual header combination. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/SharedArrayBuffer#security_requirements

b2.note: Chrome exposes timestamp-query as an optional adapter feature to ordinary secure web content on supported platform/GPU configurations; availability is not universal across all adapters. Source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/webgpu/overview

b3.verdict: disagree: WebAssembly module validation is a format/type-validation operation and is not itself conditioned on cross-origin isolation. However, instantiating or creating shared WebAssembly.Memory requires usable SharedArrayBuffer, which requires cross-origin isolation in web content.

rows.claim: A cross-origin embedded page cannot unilaterally obtain cross-origin isolation: the top-level document and embedding policy must cooperate, and the iframe must satisfy applicable COEP/Permissions Policy. WebGPU itself is available to a secure embedded document when the embedding Permissions Policy permits it; it does not inherently require cross-origin isolation.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN Permissions-Policy: cross-origin-isolated; Chrome WebGPU embedded-context test
rows.notes: Chrome additionally documents credentialless iframes as an embedding aid, but credentialless does not let an arbitrary child unilaterally make itself cross-origin isolated.
